newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Minister asks Yeltsin to suspend him amid scandal.
newsitem.headline: Minister asks Yeltsin to suspend him amid scandal.

text.p: Russia's justice minister said on Saturday he had asked President Boris Yeltsin to remove him from office temporarily amid a scandal over a video film alleged to show the minister in a night-club sauna.

"I have asked the president of the country, B.N. Yeltsin, to suspend me from my duties as a minister until all the circumstances (of the controversy) have been clarified," Valentin Kovalyov said in a statement issued by his ministry.
It was not immediately clear whether Yeltsin, who was in the United States for a world summit in Denver, had responded to the request -- a highly unusual step in Russian politics.
The monthly Sovershenno Sekretno (Top Secret) newspaper published grainy photographs taken from the video which it alleged showed Kovalyov in a sauna with women.
"I am not aware of anything I have done that I should be ashamed of," Kovalyov said in the statement.
He said his main aim in seeking to be suspended from office was to preserve the reputation of the Russian government. But he also said he would defend his own "good name, honour and dignity".
